title: Planckian Selected for €10 Million ($11 Million USD) EIC Accelerator Blended Finance Package to Scale Shared-Control Superconducting Processors
excerpt: Planckian, an Italian superconducting quantum hardware developer, has been selected for the European Innovation Council (EIC) Accelerator, securing €10 million ($11 million USD) in blended financing. This funding will support the development of their shared-control superconducting processor architecture, which aims to overcome scaling limitations of conventional quantum computers. The company plans to use this investment to transition its design into an externally accessible quantum computing system.
content:
Italian superconducting quantum hardware developer Planckian has been selected for the European Innovation Council (EIC) Accelerator under its GLOBAL-Q project, securing a €10 million ($11 million USD) blended financing package to advance its processor architecture toward commercial deployment. Selected as one of 35 deep-tech companies from 453 full applications across Europe, Planckian will receive a €2.5 million ($2.75 million USD) EIC grant for a 24-month development program alongside a planned €7.5 million ($8.25 million USD) equity investment from the EIC Fund timed with the company’s upcoming Series A round, subject to standard due diligence and grant agreement finalization.

Conventional superconducting quantum computers require dedicated control lines routed from room-temperature electronics into dilution refrigerators for each individual qubit, creating severe thermal, cabling, and cost bottlenecks as processor counts increase. Founded in 2023 as a spin-out of the University of Pisa and the Scuola Normale Superiore with operations in Pisa and Milan, Planckian develops a globally driven superconducting architecture in which multiple qubits share common control lines to decouple control-plane complexity from qubit scaling.

The EIC selection follows Planckian’s inclusion in September 2026 as one of 13 companies chosen for the EuroHPC Quantum Grand Challenge. Under the 24-month EIC work program, led by Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Michele Dallari and Chief Operating Officer Jana Nurmukhanova, the company aims to transition its shared-control processor design into an externally accessible quantum computing system.
